The sixth review of 1.24.36 (commit 801fe71; 1.24.35 is 8cb3281)
=================================================================

SUMMARY
391 cases of my own (none taken from the earlier reviews), run against src/lantern.inner.html at 801fe71:
313 AGREE, 78 DISAGREE -- 51 high, 23 medium, 4 low.
  node tests/fixtures/review6_1236/replay.js [file]    (output: run_801fe71.txt)
Both guards agree: every bench prompt equals 1.24.35's except make-control and make-control-b, and all 1139 saved
replies with a MAKE block in tests/fixtures/bench_run_*.json build exactly as on 1.24.35.

The high findings fall into nine groups. Six are Lantern's own givens shown for a question they do not fit. Two are code
checks that send back a right circuit, with a line that builds wrong. One is the user's kept circuits being matched
on loose word overlap. The pattern is the same every time: a word that changes the circuit is read as fitting.


HIGH
----
H1  The control voltage: a control transformer written "primary / secondary" gives the PRIMARY as the control
    voltage.
    Cases: p-v-xfmr-240-24, p-v-xfmr-240-24b, p-v-xfmr-208-24, p-v-xfmr-120-24, p-v-xfmr-230-24.
    Seen: "a control transformer 240 V / 24 V" (also 240V/24V, 208 V / 24 V, 120 V / 24 V, 230 V / 24 V) gives
      supply "240 V AC" (208, 120, 230).
    Right: 24 V, which is the secondary, or no supply line at all.
    Cause (GIVENS_CONTROL supply()): CTRL_BEFORE matches "control transformer " right before the first number. The
      24 V after the slash is not a candidate, so the primary is the only one and it wins. "480/120 V control
      transformer" is read right, because there the voltage stands before "control".

H2  Sequence: "the second may start only when the first is OFF" gets the sequence given, which is the opposite.
    Cases: p-q-off-fan, p-q-off-motor-idle, p-q-off-pump-not-on, p-q-off-pump-fan-not-running,
      p-q-off-conv-not-running, p-q-off-unless-off, p-q-off-while-off, p-q-off-pump-idle, p-q-off-m-tags,
      p-q-off-ordinals, p-q-off-not-on.
    Seen: questions like these all get coil M2 M1, so M2 can start only while M1 RUNS:
      - "fan 2 can only start when fan 1 is off"
      - "motor 2 can only start when motor 1 is idle"
      - "pump 2 ... when pump 1 is not on"
      - "the pump can only run when the fan is not running"
      - "conveyor 2 cannot start unless conveyor 1 is off"
      - "can only run while conveyor 1 is off"
      - "M2 ... when M1 is off"
      - "the second fan ... when the first fan is off"
    Right: no given. The two must never run together, which is an interlock on M1's closed contact.
    Cause: seqOrder() reads the order word (when, while, unless, only) but never the state the first machine must be
      in. SEQ matches on the machine's number ("fan 1", "M1", "pump 1"), so any state passes. "is stopped" is refused
      only by accident, through the block's stop-word rule. "is off", "idle", "not running" and "not on" are not
      refused.

H3  Stations: "two locations / places" is counted as two start/stop stations, whatever it was said of.
    Cases: p-s-estop-two-locations, p-s-estop-two-places, p-s-stop-two-locations, p-s-stop-two-start-one,
      p-s-stopped-3-started-1, p-s-stops-at-two-places, p-s-stops-2-start-panel, p-s-runlight-two-loc.
    Seen:
      - "an e-stop at two locations" and "an emergency stop at two places" give one e-stop and two full stations.
      - "a stop button at 2 locations", "stop buttons at two places" and "stops at 2 locations and the start at the
        panel" all give two starts as well.
      - "the stop button at two locations and the start button at one" gives two starts.
      - "stopped from 3 places but started from one" gives three starts.
      - "a run light at two locations" gives two stations and one light.
    Right: no given, or only the stops counted.
    Cause: stations() takes "(two|...) (stations|locations|places)" without asking what stands before it, and never
      reads "at one", "from one" or "at the panel".

H4  Delayed start: shown where the timer's job is not said, or is said to be something else.
    Cases: p-d-tdr-fan, p-d-tdr-pump-starter, p-d-tdr-blower, p-d-tdr-stops-it, p-d-horn-also-stop,
      p-d-power-restored.
    Seen:
      - "a fan with a time delay relay", "a motor starter for a pump with a time delay relay" and "a blower with a
        time delay relay, start and stop buttons" each get a delayed start, timed at Lantern's own 10 s. The relay
        could as well be an off-delay run-on or a run for a set time.
      - "a pump with a time delay relay that stops it" gets a delayed start.
      - "the horn sounds before start and also when it stops" gets a horn only before the start.
      - "a delayed start of 30 seconds after power comes on" is a restart delay with no buttons, but gets a
        push-button start.
    Right: no given.
    Cause: asks matches "time delay relay" and "time-delay relay" alone. The `not` list has no "that stops it", no
      "also when it stops" and no "after power".

H5  Lit button said another way.
    Case: p-l-in-button.
    Seen: "a light in the start button" gives a plain run light (lamp LT1 M1 "run" green). The fifth review mended
      "illuminated / lighted / lit button"; "a light on the start button" is refused.
    Right: no given.

H6  Sump: the alarm's red light is drawn as a pump-running light.
    Case: p-sp-horn-and-red-light.
    Seen: "a high water alarm that sounds a horn and lights a red light" gives lamp LT1 M1 "pump on" red, plus the
      horn on FS2. The light the question ties to the alarm comes on whenever the pump runs.
    Right: no given, or the light on FS2.
    Cause: read() takes "lights a red light" as a plain light (the alarm's words are not before a "with" or "and a").
      The sump block's alarm path then adds the horn only, because the question has a horn word.

H7  Code check (control-cutouts): a vacuum switch's numbers are read as pressure, and the right line is sent back.
    Cases: b-ok-vacuum-inhg, b-ok-vacuum-kpa.
    Seen: a vacuum pump's switch written "cut-in 15 inHg, cut-out 22 inHg" (or "60 kPa / 80 kPa" of vacuum) without nc
      is sent back: "a high cut-out drawn normally open ... Write it: pressure PS1 M1 nc ...".
    Why that is wrong: read as gauge vacuum, the pump must run while the vacuum is weak. That means the absolute
      pressure is high, so the switch closes as the pressure rises: no nc, as written. The line handed back runs the
      pump only once the vacuum is already deep.
    Right: nothing. A vacuum's numbers can be read either way (rule 7).
    Cause: way() trusts cut-in < cut-out for any pressure switch. NOT_AIR (with vacuum in it) guards only the BARE path.

H8  Code check (control-stops): an overload's alarm relay is judged as if it were the motor.
    Case: b-ok-overload-aux-relay.
    Seen: "overload OL2 CR5 no" with coil CR5 "motor overload relay" (a horn on CR5) is sent back as "the motor runs
      only with the overload tripped. Write it: overload OL2 CR5". Copied, the alarm relay is pulled in, and the horn
      sounds, whenever the motor is healthy.
    Right: drawn, with nothing sent back. A relay named for an overload is not a machine.
    Cause: this is the fifth review's "fault relay" class. MACHINE matches "motor" in the label, and NOT_MACHINE has
      no "overload".

H9  The user's kept circuits are shown for questions they do not fit (GIVENS sameAs()). The test is about 75% of the
    words the same, so one word that changes the circuit passes. "without" and "no" are stop words, and word order is
    not read.
    Cases: k-run-off-light, k-run-idle-light, k-run-stop-light, k-stop-run, k-stop-running, k-seq-reversed,
      k-horn-without, k-horn-no, k-fwd-plugging, k-fill-jobs-swapped, k-comp-refrig, k-comp-low, k-comp-vacuum,
      k-24dc-vs-ac, k-sump-on-off-floats, k-sump-alarm.
    Seen:
      - Light state: a kept green RUN light is shown for "a green off light", "green idle light" and "a green stop
        light". A kept red STOPPED light is shown for "a red run light" and "a red running light".
      - Sequence order: a kept "conveyor 2 after conveyor 1" is shown for "conveyor 1 after conveyor 2", which has
        the same words.
      - Without / no: a kept delayed start with its horn is shown for "without a warning horn" and "no warning horn".
      - Extra or other function:
          - A kept forward/reverse is shown for "with plugging".
          - A kept low-start, high-stop fill is shown for "the high float starts it". Lantern's own fill given refuses
            that question.
          - A kept air compressor cut-out is shown for "a refrigeration compressor", "a low pressure switch" and "a
            vacuum compressor".
          - A kept 24 V DC circuit (+ and 0 V rails) is shown for "24 V AC control".
          - A kept one-float sump is shown for "an on float and an off float" and for "... and an alarm".
    Right: none of these is shown.


MEDIUM
------
M1  "on until it starts" is never read.
    Case: p-l-until-starts.
    The changelog lists it as read. "a pilot light that is on until the pump starts" (and four other wordings) gets
    no given. POST has no "until".
M2  "stopped from two locations" adds a second start button.
    Case: p-s-stopped-from-two. This is the same cause as H3, but here only stopping is said.
M3  "a mushroom head stop button" gives an e-stop AND a stop.
    Case: p-e-mushroom-stop. The question asks for one stop button.
M4  "mechanical interlock only" gives the electrical interlock line too.
    Case: p-r-mech-only. Lantern adds that interlock between forward and reverse anyway, so it is medium, not high.
M5  "where the start button also stops it" (push on, push off) gets the three-wire starter.
    Case: p-n-start-also-stops.
M6  "a conveyor with an on-delay timer" gets the delayed start.
    Case: p-d-on-delay-timer. What the timer delays is not said.
M7  Manual or automatic sequence is not said, yet the given has a start for each machine.
    Cases: p-q-starts-once, p-q-starts-first-then, p-q-m1-first-then-m2.
    Questions: "conveyor 2 starts once conveyor 1 is running", "the fan starts first and then the pump starts",
    "M1 starts first, then M2".
M8  The stop check hands back a line that builds wrong.
    Case: b-ok-energise-stop-relay.
    Written: "stop PB1 CR2 no" pulls in a stop relay whose closed contact drops the pump. That is not fail-safe, but it
    works. Handed back: "stop PB1 CR2". Copied, CR2 is pulled in whenever the stop is not pressed, so the pump can
    never run. Right: say the stop should be fail-safe and give the whole change (stop PB1 M1), or say nothing.
M9  A fill's single float named for the EMPTY tank, written open, is drawn to run the pump only while the water is
    above it, and nothing goes back.
    Case: b-back-fill-empty-open.
    Only a stop float written open is caught. The line to write is float FS1 M1 nc "tank empty".
M10 Which code, by place.
    Cases: c-lagos, c-nairobi, c-seoul, c-mexico-comma, c-ghana, c-uganda, c-pakistan, c-egypt, c-iec-480-60.
    - "in Nigeria", "in Kenya" and "in South Korea" pick IEC, but "Lagos, Nigeria", "Nairobi, Kenya" and
      "Seoul, South Korea" fall to US. The comma form lists other countries but not these three.
    - "Monterrey, Mexico" picks IEC while "in Mexico" picks US. Mexico's NOM-001-SEDE is drawn from the NEC, so US is
      right.
    - IEC / BS 7671 countries that are not listed fall to US: Ghana, Uganda, Pakistan, Egypt, and likewise Tanzania,
      Zambia, Zimbabwe, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Dubai and others.
    - "an IEC contactor, 480 V 60 Hz" picks IEC. IEC-rated contactors are what most US panels use, and 480 V 60 Hz says
      North America.
M11 Sump alarm: "a high water alarm horn and a high water alarm light" gets the horn only.
    Case: p-sp-horn-and-alarm-light. The given is shown "as it stands" without the light that was asked for.
M12 Kept circuits.
    - Case k-estop-without: a kept e-stop circuit is shown for "without an e-stop".
    - Case k-comp-cutin: a kept switch labelled "cut-out 120 psi" is shown for "cut-in 120 psi".


LOW
---
L1  "a 2 h.p. fan" reads "2 h" as two hours, a time, so no given. Case: p-st-2hp-dots.
L2  "a forward light and a reverse light" gets no given. This plain ask is missed safely.
    Case: p-l-fwd-light-rev-light.
L3  "a Latin American customer" (and "South America") picks IEC, but the region is mixed. Case: c-latin.
L4  "a pre-start warning horn" with no time gives timer TR1 "10 s". That is Lantern's own time, copied as a setting.
    CLAUDE.md asks never to invent a time for electrical work. Case: p-d-pre-start-no-time.
L5  Not a case. A vacuum switch written nc is listed under the drawing as "checked: PS1 opens as the pressure rises",
    vouching for a reading Lantern cannot be sure of (H7).


WHAT AGREES (313)
-----------------
- Starter, plain and in many trades' words: seal-in, latching, NEMA size 1, DOL to IEC, transfer pump, barn fan, 5 HP,
  1/2 HP, 30 A, a 10 m belt, Kenya.
- The control voltage said of the control:
  - "24 V control", "control voltage 120 V", "the starter coil is 120 V", "control circuit, 120 V", "230 V coil",
    "12 V DC control", "115 V control transformer", "480/120 V" and "480 to 120 V control transformer", "24 V DC
    start/stop station", "coil voltage of 24 V AC", "400 V pump with 230 V control".
  - No supply line for a machine's voltage, for 277 V, for "on a 120 V circuit", or where two control voltages are said.
- Lights: plain, run and stop, "goes out when it starts", "shows it is stopped", colours paired with states either
  way, white, "turns off when it stops".
- No light given and no given at all for plural lights, illuminated or lighted buttons, flashing, and one light for
  forward/reverse.
- Trip, overload and power lights left out for the model.
- Stations: both ends, two and two, three, two places, local and remote, with an e-stop.
- Refused: two stops and one start, office and roof, a remote stop, "each end and the middle", two e-stops.
- Every "explain / what / why / size" question, two-wire, VFD, star-delta, hoist, heater, lights as the load, two
  machines, IEC tags, jog, key switch, a time said.
- Reversing: plain, e-stop, 24 V, "stop before reversing". The interlock is kept even for "without interlocks"
  (NFPA 79 / IEC 60204-1 9.3.4).
- Sequence order read right by name, number, number word, ordinal, M-tag, letter and reversed numbering; a chain of
  three; "must not start before"; "will not start unless".
- Sequence refused: "must not run while", "until it has stopped", a stop said otherwise.
- Delayed start with the times said: 5 s, 30 s, 15 s, 1 min, 0.5 s, "horn 5 s then"; e-stop. Refused for two times,
  run-on, and "after the pump starts".
- Compressor: cut-out read (8 bar, 125 psi, never "20 psi above"), lights, e-stop, contactor.
- Compressor refused: refrigeration, low oil, two machines, well pump, unloader.
- Fill on one float (trough, cistern from a well pump, tower) and on two floats with jobs said. Refused: from a well,
  with an alarm, reversed jobs.
- Sump with an alarm light, horn, buzzer or bell, and with a run light. Refused: plain "alarm", buzzer alone, beacon,
  low alarm, overload alarm.
- All eleven givens I built for their own questions build clean, with nothing sent back. The delayed start's
  overload is in CR1's rung, and the horn sounds only while it times.
- Code checks leave 33 right circuits from boiler, refrigeration, fire, HVAC, hydraulic, well, kiln, gas, pool,
  heat-trace, fill and sump work.
  - These include standby, freeze, fire-pump starts, fault relays, a tank-full relay, a dry-run float, energised
    alarm relays, a switch on the coil's line, `stop PB1 all`, an e-stop written open (drawn closed and said), and
    an overload light.
- The checks send back 23 wrong circuits once, each with the right line, and each line copied in place builds clean:
  - high and low cut-outs both ways;
  - a compressor's bare "cut-out";
  - stop / off / e-stop buttons;
  - a stop or overload written "no";
  - a fill's floats written open;
  - IEC practice named as 60204-1 9.3.2.
- Practice: 28 of 38 pick cases agree (including 2 saved-choice and 2 code-line cases). The user's choice decides only where nothing is named. The IEC line names 7.3,
  9.4 and 10.7.
- Kept circuits: not shown for e-stop, two stations, IEC, flashing, jog, local and remote, remote, both ends, a
  second station, HOA, a float, a timer, 24 V, a light the kept circuit lacks, a thermostat, another machine,
  empty or drain against a fill.
  Also: never while the bench runs; a circuit with a rule sent back is not kept.


NOT THIS CHANGE (seen on 1.24.35 too)
-------------------------------------
- An overload written on two lines with one ID ("overload OL1 M1" then "overload OL1 LT1 no") keeps the first line's
  closed contact. The trip light is drawn lit while NOT tripped.
- A rung whose only element is an overload contact is called "nothing switching it".
- AI_CONTROL's asks() misses some plain wordings, so they never get a given:
  - "Draw a sequence control: ..."
  - "Draw a delayed start circuit for a conveyor ..."
  - "Draw a hold-in circuit ..."
  - "Draw a ladder where motor 2 can't start unless motor 1 is already running"
  - "Draw a forward reverse control for a mixer with an e-stop and a stop button"


NOT RUN
-------
- No model (no small model, no 35B), no `npm test`, no browser. The view was checked through jsdom only. I called
  keep() and forget() directly rather than clicking "Keep as my given".
- I did not judge how the drawings look.
- Not tried:
  - a duplex pump station's own kept circuits;
  - the IEC/US button's change of the saved choice through the DOM;
  - givens for hydraulic or pneumatic circuits (none exist).
- I did not read the earlier reviews' cases or tests, as asked.
